findings.finding: The interim's outlook is likely to firm or raise FY26 expectations. The company-quoted FY26 revenue consensus of £174.1m, against H1 revenue of £91.1m, implies H2 revenue of about £83.0m, down about 2% on H2 2025's £84.8m (FY25 £163.1m less H1 25 £78.3m). Yet July revenue was +23.9%, the year to date +18.3%, August 'commencing strongly', and the largest UK competitor, Headlam, filed for administration on 1 Sep, entered it on 8 Sep and closed 28 of 76 trade counters with 154 jobs cut on 9 Sep. This will be Likewise's first statement since any of the Headlam events.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Likewise statements with strong revenue momentum were mostly paid: trading updates +7.46% (Dec-23), +12.5% (Jan-24), +11.29% (Dec-24), +4.21% (Jan-25), +8.0% (Jan-26), +4.58% (Jun-26). Reaffirm-only interims were flat to down: -3.75% (Sep-23), -0.36% (Sep-25), with +6.45% in Sep-24. The one profit shortfall (Nov-25) was -12.5%. Source: baseline history, observed RNS dates.
findings.original_quote: H1 2026 Group revenue increased by 16.3% to £91.1 million (H1 2025: £78.3 million) with a gross margin improvement of 0.7% to 32.1%. The Group has had a particularly positive H1 and looks forward to the traditionally stronger H2 and remains on track to deliver in line with market forecasts 1 ... 1 Market expectations as at the date of this announcement for FY26 (Zeus): revenue of £174.1 million, adjusted EBITDA of £11.6 million and adjusted profit before tax of £4.0 million
findings.why_not_priced: The Headlam narrative is partly priced: LIKE rose 31.67p to 35.10p on 1 Sep on about 6.4m shares, 11x average volume, and has held about 34-35p since. What is not priced is the number. No revenue upgrade has been published: the forecast stayed at £174.1m through the AGM (17 Jun) and the fundraise (28 Jul), and there has been no Likewise RNS on trading since 5 Aug. If the market held an upgraded consensus, the stock would not sit only about 4% above its 28 Jul pre-placing close of 33.5p after a +23.9% July and the removal of its largest competitor. Coverage is one house broker (analyst_count null in the baseline), so no one publishes an independent H2 number.
findings.independence: Headlam side, from different documents: administrators appointed 8 Sep (Headlam RNS via insightDIY, https://www.insightdiy.co.uk/news/headlam-appoints-administrators-updates-on-trading/16829.htm); 28 trade counters closed and 154 jobs cut (GB News, 2026-09-09, https://www.gbnews.com/money/economy-flooring-headlam-cut-jobs). Momentum since the half: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/likewise-group--like/result-of-retail-offer-and-july-update/9706662 (5 Aug: July +23.9%, YTD +18.3%, 'August starting strongly'). All of these point to the same event (the outlook paragraph), so they are merged into one finding, not two.

findings.finding: H1 profit conversion is the risk to the print. Likewise already missed a PBT forecast (Nov 2025) on 'increased costs' despite revenue growth. It only reaffirmed 'in line' at the July fundraise despite revenue running 10pp ahead of the model, cited about £0.5m of annualised extra fuel cost, and is carrying set-up costs for the Leeds 2nd hub, the Newport extension (live July), Corby, 77 new trucks and sales hiring.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last profit-line surprise was Nov-25: 'Underlying Profit Before Tax will fall short of current market forecasts' on +8.9% YTD revenue, and the stock moved -12.5%. At the Sep-25 interim, PBT +120% to £0.74m with a reaffirm moved -0.36%.
findings.original_quote: Due to increased costs and an imbalance in the revenue increases across the Group's various activities, Underlying Profit Before Tax will fall short of current market forecasts
findings.why_not_priced: Weakly unpriced. The market has rewarded revenue headlines (see the history above), and H1 PBT has never been pre-released. If investors were pricing a profit gap, the stock would not trade on about 30x forecast PBT after a +18% 60-day run. The size is small because gross profit alone rose by about £4.6m in H1 (£91.1m x 32.1% against £78.3m x 31.4%), which leaves room to absorb costs; this is a risk, not a document-backed shortfall.
findings.independence: The fuel-cost caveat and the 'in line' reaffirm despite revenue running ahead are in the 28 Jul fundraise RNS (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/likewise-group--like/proposed-fundraising-to-raise-up-to-29-2-million-/9692164), a different document from the Nov-25 warning.

baseline_tension: The finding points up while the priced lean is -0.54 (run-up 20d +10.8%, 60d +18.3%), so it cuts mildly against the lean. Part of the positive thesis (Headlam) already sits in that run-up, so the emitted +1.5 is held 0.5 below the +2.0 sum.
language_note: The UK local half here is source locality, not language, and it carried the competitor side of the story: Headlam's CVA plan, 28 trade-counter closures and 154 job cuts reached me through domestic trade and regional press (Contract Flooring Journal 3 Sep, GB News/Newsquest 9 Sep, insightDIY), not through any wire item about Likewise.

Domestic retail-investor commentary (ShareScope 18 Sep, MoneyWeek 21 Sep) had already framed Likewise as the heir to Headlam's customers. That is evidence the narrative is priced among UK retail holders, and it lowered my size rather than raising it.

The load-bearing numbers (the £174.1m consensus, July +23.9%, H1 £91.1m) are all in the RNS on Investegate, which the English wires also summarise (Investing.com/TipRanks), so the domestic sources added context, not a new number.
lessons_applied: 'Two findings resting on one document / one event are one finding': merged the stale-consensus finding (+2.5) and the Headlam-share-gain finding (+1.0) into one guidance finding, because both resolve through the same outlook paragraph. Sized +3.0 rather than +3.5.
'Financing is a question': the £32.5m placing funds a documented capacity ramp (Corby, Newport) backed by +18% revenue, so I dropped the -0.5 placee-overhang finding, which had no document behind it.

'The hunter's own caveat has to reach the number': baseline_tension cuts against the lean and the Headlam story is partly in the run-up, so expected_move is 1.5 against a 2.0 sum. The pre-lessons draft had them equal.

'Understatement is the systematic error' / thin coverage: kept the guidance finding's high end at +9 (this name's trading-update moves run +4% to +12.5%) and did not shrink it further; print_vs_bar raised from 4 to 5 because the revenue gap to consensus is mechanical.
'A truncated zero is not a zero': positioning_check says the register does not name the issuer and there is no anchor.
